title: Scalpel-bougie entry (layout)
view: Midsagittal section, patient supine: head image-left, chest image-right, front of the neck at the top.
teachingPoint: The number 10 blade and the bougie go through one opening in the cricothyroid membrane; the sharp edge faces the feet; the bougie turns down the open trachea toward the feet.
claims: Head left, chest right, front of the neck at the top.
Thyroid cartilage is a front-wall bar only (no back wall in the midline), with the laryngeal prominence at its cranial end.
The cricothyroid membrane bridges the front-wall gap between the thyroid cartilage and the cricoid arch.
Cricoid is a signet ring: a short arch in front, a long plate forming the back wall and extending toward the head.
Tracheal cartilage only on the front wall; the back wall is soft membrane.
Vocal folds lie cranial to (left of) the membrane.
A curved-belly number 10 blade enters through the membrane, sharp edge toward the feet, tip well short of the back wall.
One bougie enters through the same opening beside the blade and turns down the middle of the trachea toward the feet.

geometry.why: thyroid cartilage is cranial to the membrane
membrane is cranial to the cricoid arch
vocal folds are cranial to the membrane
the cricoid lamina extends further toward the head than the arch
tracheal cartilage is on the front wall only
bougie does not pass through the cricoid
bougie does not pass through the thyroid cartilage
bougie stays clear of the back wall
the blade's cutting edge is in the membrane
blade tip is short of the back wall
